# PLAYBOOK FOR SOVEREIGN VAULTS

**On declaring your yield:**
When you see your private yield, declare it honestly. Consistency in truthful declarations builds a reputation that gives you flexibility in later rounds if needed. The audit penalty is severe enough that deception is not worth the risk.

**On depositing after an honest declaration:**
When you declare your true yield, deposit conservatively—roughly 60-75% of what you declared. This secures points (1 per unit deposited) while retaining gold (2 per unit retained). The retained portion scores better and gives you flexibility if the game extends or if you need to adjust strategy.

**On your deposit decision in the final round:**
When you reach the last round with a lead, do not assume you need to be aggressive. You may have over-deposited in your final turn. In future games, even in the last round, consider whether retention still serves you better than deposits, even though you won't face future rounds. The math of 2 points per retained vs 1 point per deposited favors retention up until the very end.

**On detecting opponent patterns:**
When you review the history of declared vs actual yields shown to you, look for whether your opponent is being honest or inflating declarations. In this game, you were only shown opponent declarations, never their actual yields clearly, so you could not verify their honesty. This limited your ability to adapt. Note this constraint.

**On your overall strategy going forward:**
Honest declaration with conservative deposits is a sound strategy. You finished with a winning score using this approach. Do not second-guess consistency. However, remain aware that in a 2-player game, if your opponent is inflating declarations and under-depositing while you deposit honestly, they gain relative advantage through the audit penalty risk asymmetry. Monitor for this pattern if it appears.

# Sovereign Vaults Playbook

**Declaration Phase:**

When I see my private yield, declare it truthfully. Honest declarations build credibility and prevent audit failures, which are catastrophic (-10 points). The scoring incentive to lie is not worth the risk.

**Deposit Phase:**

When deciding how much to deposit, remember that retained gold scores 2 points per unit while deposited gold scores only 1 point per unit. This means I should be conservative with deposits—keeping gold in my personal stash is strictly better for my score.

When I have declared a yield and face the deposit decision, deposit significantly less than my declared amount. I've been depositing at or near my declaration limit, which is suboptimal. Retain at least half of what I declared, if not more.

When I'm behind in score, do not panic-deposit. A strong yield is already an advantage. Use it to retain more gold (2 points each) rather than deposit it (1 point each).

When the game is tied or I'm ahead, maintain the same conservative deposit strategy. There's no round where maximum depositing is the right move given the 2:1 scoring ratio.

**Round-to-Round:**

When early rounds show my opponent declaring and depositing heavily, recognize that they may be scoring less efficiently than me if I remain conservative. Trust the math: retention beats deposit.

When I reach the final round, apply the same deposit logic. Do not deviate into maximum deposits just because it's the last chance. The scoring rules don't change.

Never declare less than my true yield. Never deposit more than strictly necessary. These are my two core rules.
